main_text.p: a In benedict. terra pasc[?].[illegible, ~20 letters]b Lib.2.de Tri- nit.ca.8.[illegible, ~20 letters]c Lib.4 in Ec- clesiast.c.1.[illegible, ~20 letters]d In psal. 18.[illegible, ~20 letters] paucis, quæ sunt obseruatione digna: 1. fidem nemo habet à se, contra Pelagianos 2. fides est gratia: ergo gratia non oritur ex operibus, contra pontificios 3. hanc gratiam habent fideles, vt possint benepromereri in præsenti, ergo voluntas promerendi efficitur gratia, non autem gratia ex voluntate, & dispositione promerendi, sicut dicunt pontifici 4. gratiam facit, vt promereamur, sed non ex meritis: locutio Bedæ obseruanda, qua luculenter ostendit, antiquos patres quum merendi, & promerendi verbis vtterentur, non illud voluisse, quod volunt Pontificii, quia merendi & promerendi verba retinent; patres & merita reiiciunt, mereri significat antiquis sine merito obtinere. Sic Gregorius a 6 necessarium Adæ peccatum, o felix culpa, quæ talem ac tantum meruit habere redemptorem, hæc ille. Frustra igitur, & futiliter ex merendi verbo patrum sententiam de merito concludunt pontificii, quia mereri nos docent patres sine merito, quia & peccatum dicunt meruisse.

Alcuinus b Ex quo primum homo libero arbitrio venundatus est sub peccato, inde mala cœpit esse libertas hominis, quia ipsi libero, ablata est bonitas voluntatis, quam exinde nemo à se habere potuit, nisi gratia diuinæ misericordiæ adiutus habuisset. c Ranus: Homo non tam aliter saluari potest, nisi per gratiam Iesu Christi, videlicet sui redemptoris. Hactenus testimonia patrum posuimus, sequuntur quos pontificii inter suos numerant, quitamen cum illis in hac re nihil habent commune.
Remigius: c Cœli enarrant gloriam Dei hanc scilicet, quod non ex operibus, quæ fecimus

page.notes: The first note line "In benedict." and the second line of note a are read as printed, but the end of note a is doubtful. The running text at the right edge is too faint and too cut off to read; the fragments of the lines are left as illegible. The underlined letter at the lower right edge is not read. The right-hand printed page is cut off at the scan edge; only word fragments remain, and they are transcribed as far as they show. Marks a, b, c and the inline numbers 1 to 4 sit in the text and have no printed notes on this part. The reading of "Sic Gregorius a 6" is doubtful. The strip of the right page is not a paragraph and is not reliable in its order.
